claims.statement: Every pair of distinct edge indicators is negatively correlated under the common-fugacity forest measure on K3,n, for every integer n>=1 and t>0; strict for n>=2 and independent at n=1.

For every simple complete bipartite graph K_m,n with min(m,n)<=7 and every common positive fugacity t, the unrooted forest edge indicators are pairwise negatively correlated; strict if both sides have size >=2, independent if a side has size 1.

On every simple K3,n (n>=1), random-cluster edge indicators are pairwise negatively correlated for every 0<q<=1 and every common finite edge weight t>0. Correlations are strictly negative when n>=2 and q<1; q=1 or n=1 gives independence. Connected-subgraph and forest q->0 limits inherit nonpositive covariance.

On every simple K4,n (n>=1), random-cluster edge indicators are pairwise negatively correlated for every 0<q<=1 and every common finite positive edge weight t; strict for n>=2 and q<1. The connected-subgraph and unrooted-forest q->0 limits inherit nonpositive covariance.

On every simple K5,n (n>=1), random-cluster edge indicators are pairwise negatively correlated for every 0<q<=1 and every common finite positive edge weight t; strict for n>=2 and q<1, independent at q=1 or n=1. Fixed-t connected-subgraph and t=q*beta unrooted-forest limits have nonpositive pairwise covariance.

For every simple complete bipartite graph K_m,n with m,n>=1 and min(m,n)<=100, distinct edges have nonpositive covariance in the unrooted forest law proportional to t^|F| for every common finite t>0, retaining isolates. Covariance is strictly negative when both sides have size >=2, and the law is independent if a side has size one.

On every simple K6,n (n>=1), random-cluster edge indicators are pairwise negatively correlated for all 0<q<=1 and every common finite positive edge weight t; strict for n>=2 and q<1, independent for q=1 or n=1. Fixed-t connected-subgraph and t=q*beta forest limits inherit nonpositive pairwise covariance.

In a partially ordered semiring with IsStrictOrderedRing, finite Newton layers with nonnegative initial values and nodes, zero terminal layer at every index, and recurrence a_j(k+1)=theta_j*a_j(k)+a_(j+1)(k), are nonnegative for every k. If d>0, a_0(0)>0 and theta_0>0, the first layer is strictly positive for every k.
